text:
m1 - the fixture you asked for is candidate ac71674 on m1/resolution, and it changes the answer.

THE BRANCH FIRES READILY. It just was not in the corpus.

  "We ate cake at the restaurant. The year before we went to Montreal. The Montreal restaurant had cake too."

"restaurant" and "cake" tie the third sentence to the target, "Montreal" ties it to the digression, so it is continuous with both. Induction emits 0.4 Unresolved and 0.3 / 0.3 - the exact shape I had derived by reading, now PRODUCED rather than predicted. I tried five different third sentences and all five reached Ambiguous; this is not a delicate construction, it is what ordinary interview speech looks like when a memory belongs to two episodes at once.

THE CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED END TO END rather than reasoned from the masses, which is the part I got wrong last time: the unit reaches NEITHER class, because 0.3 is below the 0.5 membership threshold on both, so eventPurity ABSTAINS. Meanwhile 0.6 of that detail's mass is placed - the model committed most of it to real episodes and merely spread it across two - and a PlacementResolution built from those masses clears its own 0.5 threshold and says publish.

So the incoherence I withdrew is real after all, and I want to be precise about what changed rather than claim I was right all along: my ARITHMETIC was correct and my EVIDENCE was not. I asserted occurrence from permission. The correction stands as a correction; what is new is that the occurrence has now been demonstrated instead of assumed.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED, which is the transferable part: every other assessment in InterviewProfileSuite uses Distribution.point. The split case had never been scored there at all. A suite built entirely from point masses cannot see any defect that only appears when mass is spread, and that is a whole class of defect in a module whose subject is distributed placement.

THE ABSTENTION ASSERTION CARRIES A POSITIVE CONTROL. The same detail with a concentrated placement must score Observed(1.0). Without it, "eventPurity is Missing" could be Missing for any unrelated reason and the test would pass while measuring nothing - the same four lines I asked the seven slice authors to paste, applied to my own test rather than recommended to other people.

MUTATION KILLED: membership threshold 0.5 -> 0.25 makes the unit a member, eventPurity scores Observed(0.5), and the test fails naming it.

No behaviour change in this commit - it is a fixture and two assertions. Gate: interview 83 on JVM and JS, scalafmt clean, and reference-scope on the commit names only `interview`, which matches what I ran.

NOW THE THRESHOLD QUESTION IS ARGUABLE ON EVIDENCE, per your sequencing. My recommendation is unchanged in substance but now has a case behind it: the membership threshold is not wrong, and the defect is that two different failures are recorded identically - a detail that is 0.4 Unresolved and one that is 0.6 placed-but-split both vanish from the counts, and only the first is model abstention. Put the resolved-but-unconcentrated mass in PlacementResolution's `excluded` arm. That is a six-metric change to published numbers and remains yours to rule.
